narrative:
The model estimated an 88.3% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, among applicants with a profile like yours, failure is expected far more often than success; because the law school uses that risk as an admission signal, your application was denied.

The strongest driver was your third-year class-rank decile: you are in the lowest decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile. That placed you far below the admitted class and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year decile was the second-most influential factor; you were also in the lowest decile there, compared with an admitted average near the sixth decile, reinforcing the same concern about sustained academic performance. Your LSAT score was the third key factor: 32 versus an admitted average of about 37, which added further weight toward likely bar-exam difficulty.

To improve a future application, focus on the factors you can change. Prepare seriously for the LSAT and consider retaking it for a higher score; seek academic advising and, if possible, take additional rigorous coursework to demonstrate readiness. Ask admissions offices for feedback, consider schools or pathways where your current record is more competitive, and reapply only after showing meaningful improvement.
